subject: Hearthstone Health — compliance carveout & activation timeline
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Walters <sam.walters@hearthstonehealth.com>, procurement@hearthstonehealth.com
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 7 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Hearthstone compliance carveout request — initial ask

Sam / procurement team — thanks for the call today. To summarize Hearthstone's must-haves from procurement and security so we can align internal stakeholders and a delivery timeline: 

- Residency: all PII and inference logs for the Hearthstone trial must stay in US regions only (no cross-region backups).
- Audit exports: customer needs scheduled, on-demand export of full request/response traces and auth logs with retention for 365 days.
- Activation guarantee: we need predictable latency for peak batch processing (blackout windows around claims runs). Hearthstone is asking for a warm-pool reservation or routing carveout for a single dedicated tenant slice for the pilot.
- Timeline: Procurement has an internal deadline to sign by 12/15; they want a pilot start 1/4/2028.

I've attached the Security Exhibit and our latest SOW draft (SOW-draft-v2.docx) that procurement shared as the starting point. Please let me know what level of engineering/PM commitment is required to get a canary in the dev cluster by 11/30 (Hearthstone expects a demo to their security team the first week of December).

Thanks — Grace

--
Grace O'Connor
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0134

Attachments: Hearthstone_Security_Exhibit.pdf, SOW-draft-v2.docx

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Walters <sam.walters@hearthstonehealth.com>, procurement@hearthstonehealth.com
Date: Mon, 8 Nov 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hearthstone compliance carveout request — clarification and proposed scoping

Thanks Grace — looping product/eng in. Quick clarifying questions from my side before we evaluate prioritization: 

1) For "resident in US only" — do they require physical-only controls (on-prem-esque) or is a cloud-region restriction (US-east/US-west) sufficient?
2) Audit exports: do they need a self-service scheduled export (automated daily dumps to their S3) or will a manual on-demand export to a shared S3 be acceptable for pilot?
3) Warm pool: are they asking for reserved GPUs (dedicated capacity) or a routing tag that prioritizes requests to a warm pool during claims runs?

Proposed narrow scope to reduce lift and still meet procurement: 
- Deliverable A (priority): Routing tag + tenancy-affinity control that guarantees routing to US-only capacity + admin flag to enable warm-pool behavior for the tenant. (This solves residency + predictable warm path without full infra carveout.)
- Deliverable B (lower lift): Scheduled audit export to an S3 endpoint we can provision temporarily (manual run until infra automation is ready).

If Eng confirms feasibility, we can propose a canary plan for 11/30 and a pilot GA of 01/04. Jonas — can you give rough effort and any blocker notes? Ben / Grace — what is the minimum acceptable compliance posture for procurement to sign the SOW?

-Jasmine

--
Jasmine Liu
Product Manager, Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.ai

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Walters <sam.walters@hearthstonehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Nov 2027 16:26:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hearthstone compliance carveout request — feasibility and timeline

Jasmine / team — short answer: scoped approach looks doable but with pre-reqs. Summary of the proposed plan and estimates: 

Plan 
1) Tenant routing tag + residency enforcement (US-only): implement routing-layer flag that pins tenant requests to US pools and a fallback that returns 503 if no US capacity is available. Estimated work: 3 devs x 2 sprints (~4 weeks) for routing + config + tests.

2) Warm-pool behavior for tenant: implement a prioritized queue + reserved slot in the warm pool for the tenant (configurable window). This is the higher-effort piece because it touches autoscaler and scheduler. Estimated work: 2 devs x 2 sprints (~4 weeks) but can be run in parallel with routing work — overall 4–6 weeks if parallelized.

3) Audit export (365-day retention + scheduled dumps): engineering effort small. We can add an export job that writes to customer S3 and rotates retention as metadata. Estimated work: 1 dev x 1 sprint (~1–2 weeks) plus security review for keys/role.

Blockers/notes:
- We will need infra capacity commitments (reserved nodes) for the warm-pool; that may require finance approval if it increases monthly spend.
- Security will need to sign the export pattern (IAM roles and KMS keys) — I can draft an implementation stub for review (attaching short plan).
- Canary by 11/30 is aggressive but possible if we scope the canary to routing + manual export and defer automated warm-pool to a follow-up sprint.

If you want a firm commitment to present to Hearthstone's procurement: routing + manual export can be delivered as a canary by 11/30 with a targeted GA for the full warm-pool behavior by 01/04, assuming finance/security approvals.

— Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

Attachment: hearthstone_impl_plan_stub.md

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hearthstone compliance carveout request — ask to prioritize (business impact)

Team — quick business context to prioritize this: Hearthstone is a potential $1.2M ARR first-year deal (pilot -> paid rollout). Procurement has indicated that the compliance controls above are gating exec approval. If we miss the 12/15 signature they will likely push to a competitor.

Ask: Can Product/Eng treat the routing + manual export canary as a fast-track item and commit to a go/no-go for canary by EOD Friday (11/12)? If we get a yes, I will escalate budget for the short-term reserved nodes and sign-off on the procurement side to speed KMS approvals.

If routing + manual export can be demoed 11/30 we keep the 1/4 pilot target. I appreciate the tight timeline — happy to coordinate any pull requests, acceptance criteria, and to help staff QA on the customer side.

Ben

--
Ben Carter
Director, Enterprise Sales (West)
ben.carter@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0199

From: Sam Walters <sam.walters@hearthstonehealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@hearthstonehealth.com, jasmine.liu@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 10 Nov 2027 15:44:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hearthstone compliance carveout request — confirmation and pilot start

Grace / team — thanks for the quick follow-up and the proposed scope. Procurement confirmed that the narrow-scope approach is acceptable for signing the SOW as long as the canary demonstrates routing to US-only capacity and we receive a one-time export of the last 90 days for their security review. They will accept a manual export for the pilot; automated scheduled exports can be in the GA scope.

Next steps from Hearthstone: 
- We can sign the SOW next week if Redwood provides a short written commitment: canary demo by 11/30 and an export of 90-day traces no later than 11/30.
- Pilot start target of 01/04/2028 works for our onboarding team.

Please advise on any documentation you need from us (S3 destination info, KMS ARNs). I will also share our internal acceptance checklist to help QA the canary.

Sam Walters
Head of IT Security, Hearthstone Health
sam.walters@hearthstonehealth.com
